Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ims.tutorials (development version)

  • Every Summary’s first exercise is now a final render, commit and push, answered with the URL of analysis.qmd on GitHub, in place of the whole-file show_file("analysis.qmd", start = 0) paste. The separate repo-URL exercise is gone; the file URL contains it. Each tutorial is one exercise shorter.

ims.tutorials 0.0.0.9004

  • Knowledge drops now show the book’s own diagrams: 63 figures across 21 tutorials, such as the tree of variable types in Hello Data, the sampling pictures in Study Design, and the randomization and bootstrap schematics from Chapter 11 on. Plots of the chapters’ data are never copied. Students build those.

  • The tutorials copy the book’s sentences as their own prose, without quotation marks, and credit the book once, in the last paragraph of each Summary. Each chapter’s own summary paragraph is now plain text, not a block quote, with “chapter” changed to “tutorial”, and trimmed where it described material the tutorial never covers (Chapters 4, 7, 18, and 19). The figures and sentences stay under the book’s CC BY-SA 3.0 license, recorded in inst/COPYRIGHTS, LICENSE.md, and the DESCRIPTION Copyright: field.

  • Help-page exercises (?dataset) are cut to one in each of the first three tutorials and none after. Caching exercises are gone from every tutorial: students learned caching earlier, and these tutorials teach statistics. Tutorials are about four exercises shorter as a result.

  • Knowledge drops are shorter and plainer throughout. The Introduction no longer says “You may need to restart this tutorial after you do so,” which learnr2 does not require.

  • Fixed Summary answers that did not match the student’s finished analysis.qmd, in several tutorials: a missing chunk, or a chunk the student had already replaced.

  • New tests check that every image a tutorial references exists and is used, that every tutorial credits the book’s license, and that no tutorial caches or has more help-page exercises than allowed.

  • Tutorial directories no longer carry a chapter-number prefix (hello-data, not 01-hello-data); each tutorial’s place in the list is the ordering: field in its YAML header, read by learnr2 0.1.3. Chapter 7 is linear-regression-single and Chapter 8 linear-regression-multiple, keeping package paths under the 100-byte limit for portable tarballs.

  • Code blocks follow learnr2’s convention: commands are tagged with their language, expected output is tagged {.output}, and displayed chunks use {verbatim} blocks instead of <pre><code>.

  • Each tutorial’s Summary now quotes the chapter’s own Summary paragraph, for the chapters that have one.

  • Added six tutorials, the companions to Chapters 11 through 16: Hypothesis Testing with Randomization (hypothesis-testing-randomization), Confidence Intervals with Bootstrapping (confidence-intervals-bootstrap), Inference with Mathematical Models (inference-mathematical-models), Decision Errors (decision-errors), Applications: Foundations (applications-foundations), and Inference for a Single Proportion (inference-for-a-single-proportion).

  • Added eleven tutorials, the companions to Chapters 17 through 27, so every chapter of the book now has one: Inference for Comparing Two Proportions, Inference for Two-Way Tables, Inference for a Single Mean, Inference for Comparing Two Independent Means, Inference for Comparing Paired Means, Inference for Comparing Many Means, Applications: Infer, Inference for Linear Regression with a Single Predictor, Inference for Linear Regression with Multiple Predictors, Inference for Logistic Regression, and Applications: Model and Infer.

  • Added cherryblossom and palmerpenguins to Suggests, for run17 in Chapter 19 and penguins in Chapter 25.

  • Every tutorial now uses only its own chapter’s data. Study Design replaces malaria, which Chapter 2 never uses, with the stent study it discusses, and Applications: Explore replaces county with Chapter 6’s company expenses and its real 2010 Duke hiring counts. Chapters that give data only as counts ship them as CSVs in inst/extdata/, and test-downloads.R now checks every such file.

  • Trimmed the knowledge drops that ran past two sentences.

  • Added infer to Suggests, used by the simulation answer chunks from Chapter 11 on.

ims.tutorials 0.0.0.9002

  • Tutorial directories drop their two-digit chapter prefix (01-hello-data is now hello-data); each tutorial’s YAML header sets learnr2: ordering: to its chapter number instead, which fixes its place in the tutorial list.

  • Added five tutorials, the companions to Chapters 6 through 10 of Introduction to Modern Statistics: Applications: Explore (06-applications-explore), Linear Regression with a Single Predictor (07-linear-regression-single), Linear Regression with Multiple Predictors (08-linear-regression-multiple), Logistic Regression (09-logistic-regression), and Applications: Model (10-applications-model).

  • Applications: Explore has students download the chapter’s Brexit poll from inst/extdata/brexit.csv. A new test checks that the URL works and that the tutorial’s own copy matches it.

  • Added broom and scales to Suggests, used by the new tutorials’ answer chunks, and httr2, used by the download test.

  • Every question now locks once submitted (type = "reflection"), and its text carries the whole instruction, such as running show_file("analysis.qmd") and pasting the result. This follows learnr2’s “submit once, then locked” rule. Students must also submit each question before the next Continue button works. Only the minutes question stays editable.

  • Removed the Histograms tutorial (06-histograms) merged in pull request #2. It duplicated Chapter 6’s slot, which belongs to Applications: Explore, covered ground Exploring Numerical Data already covers, and used in-browser exercises and editable answers that this package does not. Its CLAUDE.md section, which said learnr2 has no show_file(), was dropped too. The tutorial remains in the git history.

  • Renamed the package from stat101.tutorials to ims.tutorials, matching the GitHub repository.

  • Added four tutorials, the companions to Chapters 2 through 5 of Introduction to Modern Statistics: Study Design (02-study-design), Applications: Data (03-applications-data), Exploring Categorical Data (04-exploring-categorical-data), and Exploring Numerical Data (05-exploring-numerical-data).

  • Added ggridges and maps to Suggests, for the ridge plot in Exploring Categorical Data and the county intensity map in Exploring Numerical Data. The student devcontainer image already carries both, via misc.tutorials.
